mcqs.q: The four principal components of the periodontium are:
opts: Gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum and alveolar bone
mcqs.explain: The periodontium consists of gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum and alveolar bone — together providing tooth support.

mcqs.q: The normal clinical probing depth of the gingival sulcus is:
mcqs.explain: The gingival sulcus is a V-shaped crevice with a normal clinical probing depth of 2–3 mm; it barely admits a periodontal probe.

mcqs.q: Attached gingiva is:
opts: Firm, resilient and tightly bound to the underlying periosteum
mcqs.explain: Attached gingiva is firm, resilient and tightly bound to the underlying periosteum.

mcqs.q: The line that demarcates the attached gingiva from the loose, movable alveolar mucosa is the:
mcqs.explain: The mucogingival junction demarcates the attached gingiva from the relatively loose and movable alveolar mucosa.

mcqs.q: The interdental gingiva (papilla) occupies the gingival embrasure and may be shaped as:
mcqs.explain: The interdental gingiva occupies the gingival embrasure and can be pyramidal or col-shaped; it is absent where the proximal contact is missing.

mcqs.q: Frenum attachments are folds of mucosal tissue (often with muscle) that:
opts: Join the movable mucosa to attached or specialized mucosa
mcqs.explain: Frena are folds of mucosa (often including muscle fibres) joining movable mucosa to attached/specialized mucosa — e.g. the maxillary, mandibular and lingual frena.

mcqs.q: The alveolar bone proper includes the cortical plates and the:
mcqs.explain: The supporting (alveolar bone proper) consists of the cortical plates and the intervening spongy bone.

mcqs.q: On a radiograph, the lamina dura appears as:
opts: A dense radiopaque layer lining the tooth socket
mcqs.explain: The lamina dura is a thin, dense radiopaque cortical layer lining the socket; it gives attachment to the principal PDL fibres and is continuous with the alveolar crest.

mcqs.q: A normal alveolar crest level is no more than ___ from the CEJ of adjacent teeth:
mcqs.explain: The alveolar crest is considered normal when it is not more than 1.5–2 mm from the CEJ; it is continuous with the lamina dura and forms a sharp angle.

mcqs.q: Rounding of the alveolar crest (loss of its sharp angle) suggests:
mcqs.explain: A sharp crest angle is normal; rounding of the crest is a sign of periodontal disease.

mcqs.q: On a radiograph, the PDL space appears as a radiolucent line that is:
opts: Widest coronally and slightly narrower at the apex
mcqs.explain: The PDL space (mainly collagen) is a radiolucent line between the root and lamina dura; it is widest coronally and slightly narrower at the apex.

mcqs.q: The colour of healthy gingiva is:
mcqs.explain: Healthy gingiva is coral/salmon pink, determined by vascular supply, epithelial thickness/keratinization and pigment-containing cells.

mcqs.q: Compared with gingiva, the alveolar mucosa is red because it is:
opts: Thin, non-keratinized, with many blood vessels in the connective tissue
mcqs.explain: Alveolar mucosa appears red because its epithelium is thin and non-keratinized and its connective tissue is richly vascular.

mcqs.q: The surface texture of healthy attached gingiva is described as:
mcqs.explain: Healthy gingiva has a matte, stippled (orange-peel) surface; stippling is less prominent on lingual surfaces and varies with age.

mcqs.q: The contour of a healthy gingival margin is:
opts: Scalloped, knife-edged, with sharp pointed papillae
mcqs.explain: Healthy gingiva has a scalloped, knife-edge margin with sharp, pointed interdental papillae.

mcqs.q: Loss of stippling, with a smooth shiny surface, indicates:
mcqs.explain: In disease the gingiva becomes smooth and shiny with loss of stippling (versus the matte, stippled healthy state).

mcqs.q: In inflammation, the consistency of the gingiva typically becomes:
opts: Soft and oedematous (easily deflected by air/instrument)
mcqs.explain: Inflamed gingiva is often soft and oedematous and is easily deflected from the tooth; it may also become firm and fibrotic in chronic cases.

mcqs.q: A probing depth of more than 4 mm indicates a:
mcqs.explain: A gingival sulcus is ≤3 mm; a probing depth greater than 4 mm indicates a periodontal pocket.

mcqs.q: When probing, the recommended technique is to:
opts: 'Walk' the probe circumferentially around the tooth
mcqs.explain: The probe tip is kept against the tooth and 'walked' circumferentially to explore the entire pocket/sulcus.

mcqs.q: Bone loss on a radiograph may be classified as:
mcqs.explain: Periodontal bone loss is described as horizontal or vertical/angular, in contrast to normal bone levels.

mcqs.q: Before accurate gingival observation, the clinician should:
mcqs.explain: The gingiva must be dried before accurate visual observation; assessment then uses inspection, exploration with instruments and gentle palpation.

mcqs.q: Marginal (free) gingiva forms the soft-tissue wall of the:
mcqs.explain: The free margin of the gingiva forms one wall of the gingival sulcus, the other being the tooth surface.

mcqs.q: Where the proximal tooth contact is missing, the interdental papilla and col are:
mcqs.explain: Without a proximal contact (e.g. a diastema), there is no interdental papilla or col; the gingiva forms a smooth, rounded surface over the bone.

mcqs.q: Stippling of the gingiva:
opts: Is less prominent on lingual surfaces and varies with age
Is found only on the tongue
mcqs.explain: Stippling (orange-peel texture) is a feature of health; it is less prominent on lingual surfaces and varies with age.

saqs.q: Name the four components of the periodontium.
saqs.a: Gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum and alveolar bone.

saqs.q: Describe the gingival sulcus and its normal depth.
saqs.a: A V-shaped crevice bounded by the tooth and the free gingival margin; normal clinical probing depth 2–3 mm.
The line that demarcates the attached gingiva from the loose, movable alveolar mucosa.

saqs.q: Describe the radiographic appearance of the lamina dura, alveolar crest and PDL space.
saqs.a: Lamina dura = dense radiopaque socket lining; alveolar crest ≤1.5–2 mm from the CEJ (sharp angle); PDL space = radiolucent line, widest coronally.

saqs.q: List the clinical features of healthy gingiva.
saqs.a: Coral pink; firm and resilient; scalloped, knife-edge margin with pointed papillae; matte, stippled surface; little/no bleeding on probing.

saqs.q: How do colour, contour and surface change in gingival disease?
saqs.a: Colour red/bluish; margins rounded/rolled and papillae bulbous/blunted; surface smooth, shiny (loss of stippling); consistency soft/oedematous.
